intro_html: Cubed pork shoulder browned in flour, simmered soft with potatoes, carrots and celery, then finished with a pour of cream that turns the broth silky. This is the stew you make on a cold Sunday and thank yourself for on Thursday. It carries 38 grams of protein at about $4.87 a bowl (at everyday cost), and it tastes better on day two than it did on day one.
cost_closing_html: About $4.87 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a cream finished pork stew with the vegetables and the starch already in the pot. There is no side dish to buy and no second pan to wash.
shop_smart: Pork shoulder is the cheapest braising meat we track. It is nearly the entire cost of this recipe, so buy it when the board shows it low and freeze what you do not use in two pound blocks.
Heavy cream is the one splurge line. A pint carries the batch. If you want to shave the cost, half the cream still gives you a silky broth, just a lighter one.
Buy carrots and celery whole, not pre cut. A bunch of celery and a two pound bag of carrots run a fraction of the bagged sticks and matchsticks, and ten minutes of knife work is the only difference.
Flour, thyme, bay leaves, mustard and hot sauce are already in your kitchen. That entire flavor backbone shows up as a pantry line, not a shopping line.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork shoulder into bite sized cubes, pat them dry, and toss them with the flour, salt and black pepper until every piece is dusted.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and brown the pork in batches. Crowding the pan steams the meat instead of searing it, so give it room and take your time.
Pull the pork out and drop the butter in, then cook the diced onion, carrots and celery until they soften and pick up the browned bits.
Add the garlic, dried thyme and italian seasoning and stir until you can smell them, about one minute.
Pour in the chicken broth along with the Worcestershire, dijon mustard, hot sauce and bay leaves, scraping the bottom of the pot clean.
Return the pork, add the cubed potatoes, and simmer covered until the meat is tender and the potatoes give way to a fork.
Fish out the bay leaves, turn the heat low, and stir in the heavy cream. Let it warm through without boiling so it stays smooth.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and ladle the exact amount into each container, stirring the pot between scoops so the meat does not all settle in the last few. Every bowl lands near 665 calories and 38 grams of protein.

steps: Toss cubed pork shoulder with flour, salt and pepper, then brown it in olive oil in batches.
Cook the onion, carrots and celery in butter until softened, then add garlic, thyme and italian seasoning.
Deglaze with chicken broth and stir in Worcestershire, dijon, hot sauce and bay leaves.
Return the pork, add the potatoes, and simmer covered until everything is tender.
Remove the bay leaves and stir in the heavy cream over low heat.
